summary: High rate of 429 throttles during parallel webhook retry/backoff bursts
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports an elevated and sustained 429 error rate when their ingestion system performs parallel webhook retries after transient failures. The pattern appears only during coordinated retry waves from many short-lived workers, not during steady-state traffic.

Impact: Several of LuminaSearch's ingest pipelines see 20-40% of requests returning 429 for 10-45 minutes during a retry storm. This causes backfill queues to balloon and downstream indexing to lag. Customer is on a Dedicated pool and needs guidance to avoid reoccurrence.

Environment: Dedicated capacity (pool id: ded-us-east-17), prod, region us-east. Customer uses short-lived API keys (rotated every 6h) and a fan-out webhook retrier that spins up hundreds of parallel workers on failure.

Request: Customer asks what combination of backoff, concurrency, and tenant-level rate/quota settings will prevent tenant-wide token exhaustion and whether Dedicated pool configuration can be tuned to isolate their burst without impacting other tenants.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure an ingestion runner to fan out 300 parallel short-lived workers.
2) Each worker issues a POST /v1/generate request to the Redwood API using a short-lived key, then on any non-2xx retries immediately with jitter disabled for the first 2 attempts.
3) Introduce a transient 503 from an upstream dependency for 30s to cause simultaneous retries.
4) Observe 429 rate across the tenant shortly after upstream flakiness and lasting until token buckets refill or traffic reduces.
logs:
[2026-03-10T09:14:02Z] ingress-fanout-187 POST /v1/generate 200ms -> 503 upstream; worker retries (ID wkr-129)
[2026-03-10T09:14:04Z] gateway rate-limit check tenant TID-449 token-bucket remaining: 0
[2026-03-10T09:14:04Z] gateway respond 429 x 1200 (approx over 90s)
[2026-03-10T09:25:10Z] rate-limiter refill heartbeat +300 tokens (window delta mismatch noted)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Short-lived keys + parallel retry fanout causes per-key and per-tenant accounting to misattribute tokens, creating sudden token-bucket exhaustion.
Checked rate-limiter logs: refill cadence matched config but observed larger-than-expected drain events coinciding with key rotation windows.
Observed that health-checks and some internal monitoring probes from customer hosts were counted towards tenant quota during the spike (see gateway logs).
Confirmed dedicated pool capacity was healthy (GPUs not saturated) and serving-runtime latencies were nominal — issue is quota accounting rather than compute shortage.
workaround:
Short-term: Have customer reduce parallel worker fanout to <= 50 concurrent callers and enable exponential backoff with base 200ms and jitter for 3 attempts. Avoid coordinated key rotations during active backfills. We suggested pause-and-stagger pattern for retries. Support provided a sample retry wrapper.
Mid-term: Support can enable a temporary burst allowance for tenant TID-449 while we tune quotas.
suggested_config_changes: Enable per-route isolation for heavy ingestion routes (route-level token buckets) to separate webhooks from interactive traffic.
Increase tenant burst window temporarily (burst_tokens + burst_window_ms) on dedicated pool for scheduled backfills.
Switch customer to use longer-lived ingestion keys for worker pools and rotate using a rolling scheme to avoid synchronized expiries.
Recommend client-side exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (Full Jitter) and capped concurrent workers per host.
resolution_notes: Pending: engineering to review quota accounting when short-lived keys are presented in high fanout scenarios. Support to coordinate a one-off burst increase. No code fix yet; configuration guidance provided. Marking as In Progress until engineering validates long-term config options.
